We’ll be off to Malton Farmers Market this afternoon to grab some fresh veg ‘n meat – why don’t you two pop along and help us pick up theaurus for Auntie?

Right, so today we watched  Peter Pan , and now they're curious about Great Ormond Street Hospital. James, what did you think of the film?      I like the flying best! And the Lost Boys. Why do they have to go back to Neverland every time?      That’s a good question. It’s all about adventure and imagination. But actually, real-life kids with medical needs sometimes go to a place called Great Ormond Street Hospital in London. It's a very special hospital for children.      Oh! Do they get to play with Tinker Bell?      Well, no Tinker Bell there, but it's like a magical place for kids because they have amazing doctors and lots of toys and fun activities to help them feel better while they're there.      Why do they need to go there?      Sometimes kids need special treatment that other hospitals can’t offer. Great Ormond Street is one of the best in the world for treating children. And actually,  Peter Pan  was inspired by the hospital! J.M. Barrie, the author, became a great friend of the hospital and actually gave it the rights to his  Peter Pan  works. That way, the hospital can make money from the books and plays to help kids.      Oh! Like the film  Pan  we watched before?      Yes, that’s the same story, just a different version.  Pan , the 2015 film, is actually a prequel. It’s about Peter before he became Peter Pan and started looking after Wendy and the others.  Tinker Bell  is a separate movie series that’s animated and shows what Tinker Bell’s life is like in Neverland.      Is that the one with the fairies flying around in the forest? I liked that one too. They have sparkly wings!      And they sing songs. I remember a song called “I Believe I Can Fly” from  Tinker Bell  one time—      That’s not from the  Tinker Bell  films actually, that’s from the movie  Space Jam . But yes, the  Tinker Bell  animated films are goody for little ones and are full of songs about friendship and flying.      Can I go to the hospital and see if there are really magical doctors?      Maybe when you’re older, we could go for a visit. Just not as a patient, of course. They have adventurers too, but they wear lab coats instead of green costumes!      Can they fly? Or just wave a magic stick?

Rather annoying this, having to get up so early on a Saturday. I was just starting to get some decent sleep after the kids were out of the house last night. I’ve had trouble sleeping since we moved into this flat in Exeter. It seems the acoustics in these new developments are terrible — every time one of the cats jumps off the sofa, it feels like an earthquake.      Oh I remember that, love. Back when we lived in Taunton, we had this old bed in the spare room. We used to crash on it and didn’t hear a thing. Do you remember how we used to talk about moving even further out, maybe towards Totnes or the real countryside? That was quite the wild idea at the time, wasn’t it?      Yes! I still miss the garden in that house, and I think the kids did too. It was far enough from everything but still close when we needed to be. Now Exeter has a drive in each direction and, thanks to the M5, you can’t always rely on a 30-minute drive actually taking 30 minutes, can you?      I know — quite a contrast to when we lived in Southend. Everything was on foot or on the number 11 bus then. Mind you, I miss the sea air of that place sometimes, and the walk to the shops. No traffic, no noise. All that noise in the Exeter flat is making me miss the old days — even those days in Taunton when one of the girls used to read books aloud late into the night.      Ah, well, the house-warming comes through next month and we  will  be out of here, about time! I’m not the only one counting down the days, am I?      No, me neither. Speaking of which, have we fixed up the Christmas plans yet with your brother over in Poole? I hope he can make it. The last time we all got together was a few years ago at the old flat in Bournemouth — bless his heart, he still insists we call it “the castle.” Even if it was just a bungalow.      I spoke with him yesterday — seems like the kids are growing like weeds, and he can go. Just need to figure if your parents can make it from Taunton. I’ll give them a call before the box office closes on flights.

Rather a lot of dust in this ticket office, don’t you think?      Oh aye, I’ll not lie—could do with a bit of a tidy-up. A proper Swedish massage for the building, if you know what I mean—get the knots out of it.       Laughs softly.  Well, I’ll say he needs more than a massage. Though I’ve always found a good rub-down before bed helps my back, especially with my age.      Aye, and I don’t mind admitting I’ve had a few done at the hospice in Dudley. They even make soup there—hot, hearty stuff. You ever been to one?      Not for that, dear. I went a few times to talk to the volunteers about running a small art and pottery class. They’re very dedicated people, you know. But do they do breakfast, then?      Haha—more like dinner, you know. Anyway, I’m not looking for a long-term place yet.      That’s wise—there is something rather sad about sitting in a room full of empty armchairs and only realising it as you go in…      Oh, it gives you time to think—about estate planning, about who gets your old swivel chairs and such. Though my wife she don’t reckon they’re all that attractive.      Aye, and fair play to someone who knows what they like. I often tell people a good education for the children is the best investment you can ever make. Whether at nursery or being taught at home—I’ve had a few customers complain because their kids were nowhere near up to speed with verbal skills.      Aye, what with all the gender talk these days you barely know where you are. Women run things now, and not in the way I like.      Well, I have no problem with it. Equality is bloody essential—though I do wonder if too much waiting on them makes a fellow lose respect as time goes on.      Aye, and speaking of women—they're going to play a far bigger part in the ME event next year. The committee says it's about bringing on new lifeblood and all that.      Finally, they see it. I tried to get the council to sponsor one of my art shows at the gallery, and they looked at me like I’d asked for the moon.      Tell them to have a good Swedish shuffle up the stairs and they'll see a few things clearer.

Rather than going to Cornwall this year, do you think we could do something a bit different, Mummy? I’ve been looking at some places in the south of France. Just a few days away, maybe a little flat in Saint-Tropez or the like. It would be nice to do something a bit more grown-up and uninterrupted, you know? I’ve had to sort out three children and two husbands in my time and this new one of yours isn't even under the same roof! But I suppose if you'd like a week without me breathing down your neck, I can manage that.      Oh, Mummy! Don't be like that! I’m not saying you're a nightmare company. Then we can both have the holiday we really go for rather than just coasting along trying not to step on each other’s toes. I’m really looking forward to it, Mummy—and thank you for getting it.

Rather annoying this, isn't it, love? These supermarket prices. I had to buy tinned carrots and it were nearly a fiver for half a kilo. I used to get a decent bag for a buck back in the day.      It's truly ridiculous. We've talked about it on the forums at work — we even use the 'Shop Around' app just to find better deals on a weekly basis. Even so, sometimes the best price is still way over the roof.      Oh, and don't even get me started on the customer service, or the lack of it. I went to talk to one of the shelf fillers at the local store last week and he looked at me like I was turkey on Christmas. I just wanted to know why the sugar was overpriced.      Always used to be a good chat at the checkouts, at least. These days it's, "Next please," this and "Pay or get out," that. I remember the milkman used to chat to Mrs. Hogg up the road for half an hour once a week.      I know, I know. Anyway, moving on. Did you hear about the court case that went through last week, John? They tried a man for domestic violence and sentencing was so light – it's been on the news, and I had to confirm with my colleague at the courthouse.      Light sentencin', eh? You don't say. Justice is a joke these days. Spent my time in the bookkeeping business and I’ve seen people doing the time for flimsy cases while these violent folk walk free.      I heard about it online as well. I teach at a school where the kids are the most affected by this sort of thing. Many come from troubled homes where domestic violence is normalised. It's cruel, really, how that cycle just continues.      To be honest, I think the weather reflects it too. You'd think a few rainy days would calm things down but no, people are still getting rowdy. Last weekend, there was a police call out for a disturbance next door to a new housing development.      That's not uncommon, I'm afraid. Sometimes it's the climate or the pressure of living in a place like this — it affects people's sanity. Still, I’m trying to teach mindfulness in the classroom now, to help them manage their stress. It's helping, if slowly.

Rather annoying I couldnae go to Sicily wi’ me moom and dad this summer ‘cause they’d got to go to Barcelona for their holiday. I’d been droolin’ over those sunshine pics on their phone for weeks. Still, we’ve got stew and chips in reasonable amounts. We can pretend we’re in Sicily! Or even, dare I say it, Spain... like, without the pesky heat.      Oh, I’d rather stay in and contemplate my My turkey curry. I’ve been cooking it left-right since I moved in, to be honest. D’you know, I think I turned my kettle green with how much I’ve been using it for breakfast, no doubt about it!      Aiyaaa! I love curry too! But, you know, I’ve been a bit more into my grilled cheeses—cheese and tomato, maybe a mushroom or two—nothing fancy. Honestly, I’ve been so busy with early shifts at the hospital, I’ve been falling asleep on the bus. I dream about being on Bedlinog beach – Mate, have any of you even been to Wales? It’s beautiful. Golden sands and everything. Mate, you lot should come for a weekend sometime.      Oh, I’ve been. I’m from Hartlepool, not that far. It’s a good spot. You can walk for miles and not see a soul. The bloody thing’s more attached to me than I realized. Poofed up like a loaf of Welsh rarebit and followed me to the bin last week. ‘Ere he comes!      Arf! We should take our pets and go on a road trip! Just me with my budgie Grumbleshaw. He’s the tiniest berk you ever did meet.      Oh please go, really need to see if your budgie can fight my toaster.      I’d genuinely pay to see that!      Y’see, I’ve made it to North Wales and back in two days once with my nan and gran, and we slept on the road, ‘cause they didn’t like to drive at night.

Rather annoying this, innit? I’ve been staring at this essay on utopian literature for like four hours... got nuffink outta it yet.      Yeah, I gotta do one for my art module too. No, not like what you’re thinking—more like how art reflects dystopian and utopian ideals. Sounds a faff really.      Yeah? I reckon that sounds a bit less mental tho. Why'd they gotta make us stretch our brains over some dusty old philosophers’ bollocks?      Blimey, sounds like you're not a fan of philosophy essays. I mean, I like a bit of the abstract, don’t get me wrong. But what’s the point if you're just rehashing ideas you don't believe in?      Ehh, I don’t know. It feels like they’ve got this idea of "proper" universities where you just read and write... but in reality, what’s the point of any of it, y’know? Like, what’s gonna happen when we’re all over the hill, and we’ve got nothing but essays written in undergrad?      Honestly? Oi! That’s not reassuring, is it? I mean, when I think about retirement... sounds like just a long, boring hangover.      Nah, nah, nah. Think of it this way—we get to be the people who can say, "I used to be young!" And the best part is, we get to be a bit of a failsafe for technology. If everything crashes and burns, we're the ones to have backed up ‘cos we took the time to play solitaire on a sundae.      Solitaire on a sundae? You sound like you’ve been reading too many forums.      Let’s not pretend you haven’t. I found you reading one about the psychological implications of simulation theory when you thought I wasn't looking.      I was just curious! Anyway, maybe after I graduate, I wanna go into some kind of visual design. Never really done proper art—just doodling and all. But I think it’d be cool to help people see the world differently.      That’s a proper way to see it. Like, if we can be the ones shaping how people feel... even if just for five seconds... that’s something.

Oy, I about blocked at yon anecdote you mentioned the other week, Martha. The one ‘bout what you said at that cabby in Brum. I know I had to cut a case study on the Swiss for ‘cause it didn't directly tie into the module readings.

Rather annoying day, wasn't it?      A bit, yeah—the seminar on Tang dynasty policies got drawn out, and by the time I sorted out my students, it was nearly time to meet you for tea. Believe me, I've been there. I know that university life is hard enough, especially when we moved out to China with a plan for 'cultural immersion' and high salaries. Still, I think at least we’re getting used to it. At least the students seem to like you, unlike mine, who all insist my accent is unpronounceable.      Please, I think the first week the class took bets on whether I was from a "tropical island" or the "Empire State." But I think it's working out now. Just wish the housing side line in the contract had been a little more accurate.

Rather than share a meal, we seem to be going in opposite directions these days. How do you feel about that, dear brother of mine?      I know, I've been working overtime a lot lately at the engineering firm. It gets tiring, you know.      Yes, I do. I remember when we both spent time at our grandparents' house every weekend. We would cook together and help decorate the rooms. Those were good times, weren't they?      Yes, those were some of the best. You always had such a good eye for furniture and decorating. I still remember how you transformed that dilapidated table into a lovely dining area centerpiece.      It was a bit of work, but worth it. I find that cooking can be the same way—transformative, if you put in the effort and make it an art, not a chore.      I agree. I've been trying a few recipes lately and even went planting some herbs in our little urban farming spot near the flat. It's actually helping reduce food waste for us.      That's adorable! I wish more young people your age cared as much about food wastage as you seem to. Speaking of, how are you pacing in your career?      Pretty good, I suppose. I still sometimes wonder if I should’ve taken the arranged marriage-like path—more like career path, you know what I mean—where someone else sets your direction for you. That often means conforming to what the market currently thinks is most lucrative.      Definitely. I think I've benefited from the work experience I had before. My company understands that industries are closing and that private ventures can help.   Speaker_2 :   Speaking of which, I watched this intense TV series about a woman pioneering a plastic bag charge to reduce waste and end up being controversial. Her struggles mirrored the challenges of a new entrepreneur in closed industries.      That sounds riveting. I love how such series can make even go-to details on topics like dowries or industrialization so relatable.      I suppose they could. That plastic bag scene reminded me of all those environmentalists at the university I met when I was studying for my postgrad.

Rather annoying that the oven’s on the blink again, isn’t it?      Oh, honestly, I told you ages ago we should’ve got it fixed. I've been threatening to call someone for weeks.      I know, I know. But it was fine when I last used it, and we’ve got bigger priorities right now.      Like a functioning fridge, perhaps? That’s the one from my parents’ house, isn’t it?      Yes, and I occasionally wonder what the outside of it looks like. But it’s getting the job done, even if it does play hide and seek with the fridge light now and again.      Touch wood, I swear it left the house this morning lit, and now I’m home in the dark and I think it turned off. Blimey, this is becoming something out of a British sitcom.      Haha, yeah. Maybe we should record it for the comedy factor. Still, at least the food’s almost ready. The fish is cooking and the veg is on the side.      Right, as long as the fish survives the oven’s fancy. I was thinking—what with it being such a dark evening again—I really miss the sunlight at this time of the day, and I know you do too.      All that winter sun business. You know what I miss the most? Getting the kids up for school at that sleepy, golden hour in the morning. Makes me a bit nostalgic for the old days.      Don’t get started on being nostalgic. That means remembering the panic of parenting, and most people about to fall off the sofa trying to baste the sprouts while arguing about who did not wash the dishes.      Fair point. But even with the chaos, those were proper ‘living’ days. Got less time for ourselves, sure, but everything was urgent and real.      And very intense. I remember my little mad dashes between meetings while you had that postdoc job of yours. That always topped the 'things I survive each day’ list.      Yeah, I miss not being glued to the coffee machine as much. Work can get a bit suffocating. And it goes on like that, each trying to keep the conversation from diving too deep while the house hums with appliances playing their part in the domestic drama.      So, anyone doing anything over the weekend? Just talk about it, over this bed of cod and semi-melted sprouts...

Rather lovely day today, isn't it? I was just thinking 'ow nice it'd be t' get down t' sea 'fore it turns all foggy agin. You know, holding the ‘baby blue tits’ I used to find on the school grounds. We used to feed 'em from our thumbs. Such a grand memory.      Aye, I remember the little blue tit you used to feed around ‘ere. I told meself one go’ I get me own place, I’d get a bird feeder.      That’d be a grand idea, Mark. Rather annoying isn't it? I swear I used the same brand of shampoo last week, and it suddenly felt... off. I mean, if you're not in a rush, go for it. But if you're like me and are running to pick up the kids by 3:15 every day, time is sacred. I tried a little bit of shopping therapy the other day—just browsed through the Websites陉      and ended up buying the cheapest hair serum going. Six pounds, no frill, but it left the kids' hair goenvironment friendly on the kids’ hair. If it works at that price, I'm in. Have you found any go-to shops lately? I might try some of the online stuff again if I can manage the logistics with the post office.

‘Ey Mark, you ain't told me ‘ow the parks in the new town 'ave worked out. I got to take some kids from the school on a visit next month, an' I dunno which one to pick. Liverpool Museum or Tate… I s'pose depends if they’re interested in history or eeny paintin’ of a tree with sore 'eadaches?’      ‘Ah, yeah, I've taken some of the homeless project lads to Tate a couple o' times. 'Ow t’think it's a good idea? Well, it's better than poundin’ vodka chips, I guess. Anyway, the buggers love the weird shapes, don’t rightly know why. But the Liverpool Museum? That’s more me sort o' thing. Tenpence to hear the story 'bout the docks and the Empire. A little local pride never did no 'arm, eh?’      'Ang on, you alright for parking there? Last time I went to the city, I didn’t see a single patch o' concrete that wasn’t a pound an’ ten, and that was in daylight. I’m scared if I land a job at the Uni and start commutin’ in from Birkenhead, I’ll have to sell me kidney just to afford a bottle o' pop an’ a sneaky chekin’ myself in.'      ‘Speaking of, you done the interview for the Masters yet? You were on 'bout it last week, what with all the essays an' the panic. You’d better rush, love. Felt like a lorry to the chin, ‘opefully I impressed ‘em. I passed me PGCE with honours, so the worst they could do was give me an E and call me ‘Roddy’ or summat. Feels like Christmas early if I get a place, y'know?’      ‘Eh, no pressure then. But serious now, if you do, you’ll ‘ave to celebrate. Me and you could take a few quid and go into town for a proper meal. Mandy’s ‘avin’ a big do next April, you in? We can get the uniforms out and all that.'      ‘I’m in, unless I ‘avta start ‘aving a baby with Mandy and everything else I’m doin’ falls over like a lorry hit a pigeon.

Rather annoying isn't it, how grown-ups think they have to glue themselves to their children every second? Mind you, I've only had them temporarily now and yet sometimes I feel like I've been microwaved by it all. Not to mention they have their own children at home.      Oh I'm with you there, and it's very well done saying that. My mother-in-law tries to do the whole "step by step policy", but every time I mention it, it comes back as some sort of guilt journey. You'd think she'd seen what being a parent really means.      Right, because of course! It's so bizarre, isn't it? One day you're stressed and needing help, and the next, they're suddenly the life coach on this ridiculous journey, knowing far more about what your life is and should be than you do. It's like, aren't you supposed to back off, not encroach more?      Exactly! And the worst bit is not being thought of, even though you're the real parent. I mean, that's why I do things, not for recognition or approval, but I can't help but feel as if I'm supplying only for two people while someone else is gathering brownie points.      That's so true. My Mate Laura faces precisely the same, and sometimes it really breaks her up. She's trying to make connections and establish her own kind of dynamic, but no one ever acknowledges that. It’s all 'what someone said in the past' or 'what my opinion is.'      You think you're looking out for your child and yourself and being solid in this new family structure, and it feels like most people about you are seeing every day as gold rather than trying to pass it on. Honestly, it's like they're corroding that independence you barely have time to build.      My goodness, that's so well put. It's like they think every explanation and solution must include a third party holding the strings. I mean, I tried once to manage things on my own while being fair and straightforward and that came as a major surprise to everyone.      At least someone somewhere took the bull by the horns and dared to say no. Sometimes I wonder how much more goody-two-shoes life would be if everyone just stepped back and gave the space that’s needed, especially for people in roles nobody ever properly explained what your actual job title was.

Rather annoying this new boxset eh? Still, easier watching this than me trying to figure out Pintrest again. I got lost on that thing when I tried to make a birthday card for my Nan last week. She said I was more use in the house when I was replying to emails for the council! Nah, you didn’t have to make a card, I would’ve handled it.      Aye, listen—my Nan’s never had a birthday as beautiful as yours. I was livid! “Blast it all, Jane, I didn’t fold them for nothing!”      I’m still not sure whether she did that on purpose, ‘cos she hates you, or if she thought it was a kebab wrapper. Either way it was a disaster. But it was   you  , trying to make your birthday a full-blown event. Like when I came to your last one and you’d got a playlist and chips with gravy. I thought you were setting up for a party of 30.      I was hoping my parents would show up or something. Just wanted it to feel like a proper do, not just sittin’ in the flat eating your dodgy cake. I have to say, though, you did rally the lads for the surprise football team bit, so I’ve got to give you credit for that.

Rather annoying that the chandelier we liked on eBay doesn't have a bulb holder for LEDs, isn't it? I was rather keen on its styling, you know? We might be better off looking for something more modern rather than pulling someone else’s light apart.      Didn’t even look at the reviews properly either — just went for the price. I  knew  I should’ve checked the specifications before getting excited about the design. My mistake, definitely. Still, enough about that. Have you had another rummage around Rightmove, love? I thought I saw a place matching our budget listed in the morning.      Yes, actually — I've been messing with the search filters ever since. I changed the location radius to 20 miles this time so we aren’t excluded from everything that’s actually within a reasonable drive.      Oh, that’s a good idea. Anyway, I found one that’s fairly roomy, and the photos look appealing — full four bedrooms and two bathrooms. It's a bit of a stretch, but not outlandish.      That  does  sound great — where’s it in St Albans? I did like the place we saw the other week, though the garden had seen better days. Still, you could make something of that. Not my first choice, but it’s fairly expansive and has two floors.      Well, if it's going to be where we raise the kids, then a few extra rooms might come in handy later on. And if the garden does need work, it could become a real bonus when the weather's nice.      True — all right, let’s have a look together. You pull up the link on your laptop so I can see what it's like without tearing the pictures from my phone screen.

Rather chilly this morning, isn't it? I needed three cups of coffee just to get out of the house.      Oh, I’m more of a tea kind of gal, personally. But this is strong stuff and quite nice. Look at the garden! The roses are coming along well. Got a bit of hail last week, but they’ve bounced back.      Yeah, I saw that. A lot of people’s plants got a bit battered, but yours are tough. It's a shame it’s still so damp inside though. Is that the new cologne or the washing powder?      No, that’s Maisie. She’s been the real diva since her spay. Just the other day, I found her asleep in the middle of the hallway – I swear she’s trying to trip up the dog I’m thinking of fostering.      Oh wait, you hadn’t mentioned a foster dog earlier! Have you ever seen something so disastrous? She trotted in when the bins were being picked up – it was chaos with the curb, and she barked at the lorry the whole time. Jokes, but for real, it’s exhausting.      A bit? I worked a ten-hour shift last week, straight through with no breaks, and I was passing out by the time I got home.      That’s dreadful, Jodie. Have you told your employer yet? We should all be looking after ourselves.      I’ve considered quitting go work in retail again, if that sounds boring. At least it's regular hours and smiling at people without being shouted at.      Maybe, but you could also look for private care jobs. I heard one in Tonbridge that pays a bit better.      Oh yes, and over this coffee we could be plotting a workforce revolution. Served my third cup to warm up for it.

Rather annoying this new research saying we're all supposed to go to sleep and wake up in sync with the sun... Like, I run a business. I’m up at seven, need to be thinking by seven-thirty. Can’t really moonlight as a grumpy bear at seven.      Oh come on, it doesn't say that exactly. I’m half convinced he's lying, but then I think—well, he's an entrepreneur too, just like me. Maybe breakfasts at 6am just happened. Reminds me of when we went camping last summer by the Rangitata River. Started so early, he was full-on walking like a sleepwalker.      Oh yes! I remember that. We got utterly lost on the way back in, didn’t we? Told you we didn’t have GPS in that stupid old utility. And remember the farmer we stopped at? He helped us, but just barely! Honestly, the man looked like he wanted to clock you for disturbing his cows.      That was rough! Honestly, I'd forgotten about that. But I’ve been trying to use those GPS apps now. I always remember when you first took a chance on that pottery firm. You flew straight in, no fear, just a notebook and good instincts.      Ah, yeah. I wasn't the best pilot—was more of an air-side empresario, delivering the goods. But I knew the routes by heart. Even when the co-pilot panicked over a broken altimeter, I just shrugged and said, “Up's always the safest direction until something tells you otherwise.”

So do you think we should base our project on the impact of consumerism on poverty in the UK? I mean, it's kind of relevant after the debate we had in politics class last week.      Yeah, that seemed like a topic that got everyone fired up. I reckon it’s also good because it connects to economics and society. It’s like, where does the money go and who gets left out?      Exactly! We could look at how big companies market stuff to people who are already struggling. You know, the ones who can barely afford rent but somehow get targeted with ads for luxury items.      And then there’s all that stuff the teachers told us about how some stores like that one near Wembley sell cheap, low-quality goods to poor families. I mean, who profits from them spending more and more in the long run?      Honestly? Probably the same corporations, just in a different way. Anyway, after all that, don’t you think the government should do something more than just tax the wealthy? They talk about helping people, but nothing really changes.      Oh, I’m tired of that whole thing. They say one thing when they’re in the news but then… nothing. My cousin got into a situation where he needed help from the council but they just said he “didn’t qualify.” That’s not support, that’s nonsense.      That’s brutal. I understand how that can make people lose faith in the system. But at least in science class we’re trying to do a bit of good. We’re working with a project that uses some kind of composting and it’s supposed to help reduce waste.      That’s pretty cool. Maybe if all projects could do something useful like that instead of just being a pain for your grade. Honestly, I’m barely even staying up to do any of this because the work is so complicated. I miss the simpler GCSE days.      Same here. I used to surf the web during study sessions, but now I just stare at the wall trying to think about how to word a sentence. Even my grandad said I’m spending more time with my head in the clouds than in books.      Pfft! Maybe he just wants go back to the day he had more hair and less work. But in all seriousness, after all that, don’t you just want to spend time with your actual friends instead of stressing over school?

Rather annoying the new recording setup, really. I’ve been trying to get this internet-based session with that typist off the radio show going. You remember that one?      Oh, yeah! “Chatting Through the Chatter,” the one that picks up mundane anecdotes. But why record it at home? Wasn't the studio in Croydon good enough?      Well, I’ve been neglecting my back far too long. The long drives gave me a right old flare-up in my knees. Mrs. Johnson was the one who suggested me chase it up with some physiotherapy. Get the spine realigned again, apparently.      What’s she been doing lately? From what you said before, she was living with some eccentric horse’s lawyer in Tenbury, wasn’t she?      I think he turned out to be an herbalist by trade. Anyway, back to me—this lady at therapy happened to suggest a micro-waist routine, you know, for core support, to prevent those sudden joint wrenches. I reckon it helps—haven’t been out of sorts for a full week yet.      You’re doing waistline and food control, then?      Not quite. I’m not about to start “dieting” – that’s been a fairly toxic word in my memory since Stratford. No, I’ve been trying to be more careful with what’s on the table. No need for that extra slice of cake, just someone being full.      You’d consider yourself quite particular now, then? Some floring-chic aesthetic sense, too?      A little! Look around, there’s a new coat I bought off Etsy for the springtime. Got the pattern to match the vibes from a house in Radcot Bridge. Properly coordinated now, and it helped unblock the weight that was just, well, burdening the joints.      So that’s all been a sort of uniformed event—get it sorted with spinal therapy, then restricting your cake, shopping for the perfect coat as reward?      Something like that. Of course, it helps to have company, but you… well you’re a bit more caught up with your own projects, aren’t you? I remember you mentioned something about wanting to work at that café in Reigate? It’s been a while since you last said something.      Yeah, I’ve been meaning to apply, but roles are tighter than usual with all the seasonal workers coming back to Surrey. I’ve been keeping busy doing errands online and shooting videos about… local places I go to.

Rather than chuck a frozen lasagne in the oven, I thought we could knock up a bit ‘o spaghetti Bolognese, eh? Y’know, proper one, with a bit o’ love in it.      No worries, I’ve got some fresh pasta in the cupboard. Got it from that place in King’s Parade today. Smells rather nice.      Oh aye? A lot o’ places ‘bout this town got fancy Italian stuff. I’ve not tried that place yet. We can give it a go once this is sorted. So, what d’ya fancy with the pasta? Red or white sauce?      What’s in the red? I’ve made that My turkey and mushroom one numerous times. Terry left the house this morning mutterin’ about mushrooms, so I’d say I’ll go for your standard Bolognese — chuck in the proper ground beef, no funny business.      That’s me lass, chuck the lot in — beef, onion, garlic, a tin o’ tomatoes, oregano, maybe a dash o’ red wine if we’ve got one left in the cupboard.      And for veggies? I might chuck in a couple of mushrooms, extra garlic, then a humble green — like spinach –?      Why not, it adds a bit o’ balance. Y’know, when me mam used to cook, she’d add a hit o’ carrot, but fair play, someone at our age probably should go for a bit o’ greens.      Fair play. Also, have you seen the latest advancements in ‘meetless’ mince? I’ve tried it once and about half-choked. I prefer real bangers in the Bolognese.      No cap. Proper Bolognese needs it. So, while I’re doin’ the chopping, you could start gettin’ the pan on. A bit o’ olive oil — slap a few fresh garlic cloves in there.      Arche, I’m already chopping as we speak. Let’s not speed it up with a speed mince whiz— do it the slow, proper way.      Now that’s the spirit! Once goin’, I’ll see if I can find a film. G’been a while since I’ve had a proper movie boxset bender.      So long as it’s not another murder mystery with someone in Cambridge. We’ve all gone round the twist this term.      Sounds good to me. Once the Bolognese’s churnin’, I’ll flick on Channel Five. G’been a while since I’ve seen 'Detectorists' — made me feel alright and slightly dirty.      ‘Detectorists’ is good, but do you feel alright now, or just slightly dirty still?

Rather skip the new horror flick everyone’s on about, personally. I’d much rather stick with old classics like  The Shining , you know? There’s just  something  about that atmosphere      Aye, can see that, I mean—some of them modern horror films make too much eeny use outta jump scares. It’s all just over-produced now. I’ve been trying to get everyone to watch  An American Werewolf in London  again, it’s a banger      Wee lassie, okay. Didn’t even know that was a big one over here. Out in Norn Iron, we’ve been watching  The Quiet Man  and  The Commitments  on the turkey again. You know, standard stuff. Nothing like this fancy American gothic vibe      Eww, no chance of me watching  The Quiet Man , died giggin’ when my aunt tried to show me it. Not a fan of Westerns. I’m more of a  Fargo  lassie meself. Good ones, real gritty—set over there, you know?      Aye, quite a different world from here, isn’t it? I tried watching some American crime shows the other day, and it all got way too dramatic for my liking.      Yeah, slap some gunpowder into a somersault and somehow you’ve got a  thriller . Out in Newry, we’d just call it a someone being full-on. Honestly, I’d rather just watch  True Blood .      Ah, now that, I can get behind. Made a decent attempt at mixing in a bit of drama and about daftness. I mean, not the best lit, but it had vibes.      Have you lot seen  Sweet Home ? It’s this South Korean horror show, like  House of the Dead  meets  Parasite . Banging visuals, man. I’d show it to you all, but I dunno how long your broadband’ll last while the trailer downloads.      Ah, yeah, I’ve been meaning to check out more international stuff. Was watching  The Platform  the other day, like a dystopian film set in a really daft prison. It’s not got much of a plot, but it’s got that brutal Spanish vibe goin’ on.      So, have any of you seen  The Banshees of Inisherin  yet? Martin McDonagh’s latest?      Aye, and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Searing and all that, but done with class.      And to think it’s set right near where I’m from! Though I’ve got to say, it didn’t really resonate with me as much as  The Crying Game , which had a bit more heart to it.

Rather annoying to be honest, Mump. I mean, I love Paris and all, but that croissant... got to my throat within ten minutes of eating it. I think it was either the sugar or the butter, but I spent the entire morning feeling like I’d swallowed a cactus spike.      Oh, I don’t think you should be saying things like that about法国 food, Alice. You should be more careful with your language in this house, even if you're used to it in the city. Still, you poor thing, sounds like it was a bit of a rough start. You'd think the bakeries in Paris couldn’t mess that up, could they?      Alice, you always manage to find something to complain about. Fun fact for you—some croissants are just denser than others, and I think the ones in Paris are often made for breaking off into smaller pieces. You probably wolfed it down too fast. Honestly, I’d be more worried about you jumping over that bridge, or ordering the wine. Also, the escalator incident still haunts me.      Well, listen—there I am in the airport, coughing and buying grief over painkillers, and there was Marcus watching it all. He’s been bugging me about it since—he says I'm a “charming, clumsy, but predictable mess” now. And he wasn't wrong. I just wish I hadn't managed to break my ankle on the Champs-Élysées.      Honestly, Alice. You went alone with your brother’s friend. You didn’t even ask me if I wanted to come. I would’ve been so much more suited to keeping you out of trouble about now. I know he's reliable, but it still worries me when you're off doing all that without any idea of what to do when things go wrong. You could’ve handled that so much better with planning beforehand.      On the bright side, I’m told the painkillers were probably strong enough to last until next week, which is when I expect your next crack-up story to start. You being clumsy adds a bit of excitement to the place.      Well, let’s talk about  your  excitement this week. How's the new project goin’, Lucy? The one you've been working so hard on.      Frankly, it’s a blooming disaster. I had to cancel my latest therapy session planning because one of the residents had a panic attack in the garden, and I’m now stuck rescheduling slots for the entire week over this one meltdown.

Right, so the first thing you gotta do is get a pan or a big pot, and put some oil in it and heat it up. Then you chuck in the onions, you know, the ones we got from the market? Not the green ones, the big brown ones. Just like my gran used to do on a Saturday when she made chicken tikka masala. I reckon it smells better than… well, a jellyfish on a beach. Not that I’ve smelt one, but you know what I mean.      Oh, I remember your gran’s cooking when you were little. She used to fetch frozen chicken from the garage,  after  it had been in the sun, and still manage to make it taste okay. Just don’t let it go off like that one time when you woke up with the hiccups and a very sad face. But how much oil are we using? And why do we need breakfast, lunch and then Curry Club in our house after 7pm?      Just a little, like a teaspoon. And I dunno, maybe because gran had a key into the curry lorry or something. Anyway, I put two slices of garlic in with the onions and a couple of chopped tomatoes. Then we simmer it for a bit. Oh, and put the rice in a separate pot with double the water. I saw a clip on TikTok where some woman said that her gran used vouchers to buy rice and curry paste. Imagine that, back in the old days, they didn’t just chuck forty jalapeños in the recipe because they fancied it.      Some things never change, I suppose. You can’t be trusted with spices if I’m not in the room. Last time I let you add “a pinch of salt,” it ended up tasting like sea water and a little bit of crying. And that was before I mentioned the time you tried to cook something that had a facial deformity from the burners. Honestly, I thought it was a failed science experiment.      That was  one  time! And I was waiting for the spoon to crack from hearing you complain. Anyway, after simmering, add the curry to the pot with the vegetables. Now, the meats… well you remember when I tried to cook the steak the other day and go it really smelly? I think it had gone off.

Rather annoying this newfit here eh?      Aye, it's mad they’re piling in so much ‘tertiary level stuff’ at Sixth Form now. I nearly dropped me phone when me maths teacher started moonlighting as a chemistry lecturer.      I don’t eeny mind it, I think it’s brilliant! At least if yer stuck on something, they don’t just let yer flounder. Not like in Germany, where me mam always said,  “Wenn’s nicht klappt, dann ist das Leben so.”  Blimey, that's a hard headbutt when yer 16.      Look at the bleedin’ point of it though. Everyone’s cramming, and no one’s talkin’ ‘bout jobs or how to get back into the system, if y’know what I mean. I did uni, but uni doesn’t pay yer breakfast, no matter if yer clever.      Oh don’t start, Liam. You lot always say the same thing. I mean, uni gave me the lot—skills, contacts, even a bookshelf full of text books I can’t read now.      It’s not that, Alice—it’s just watching Liam here, trotting out all his “I want to build a rocket” dreams while he plays FIFA and eats takeaways for dinner. No plan, no goal. Mate, you done a whole degree in what—political theory?      I did what someone said to do. If y’ain’t gonna use it, then why do it? Some nutty kid at uni told me I’d get a job in social services or education. Well, there it is in front of me—talking about you, the support worker.      I suppose you could say that. But I like it. Doesn’t pay a fortune, but it’s fulfilling, ‘cos I’m helping people. You can’t just live on dreams and Red Bull.      Oh, I know. I tried that for a year. Ended up working the Saturday rush at Greggs for a few weeks—enough to notice no one really wears suits to the shop till.      But you’re not stuck, Liam. That’s the go. Work on your own terms. Start a graphic design thing or something. You’ve got the skills, don’t go lying bloomin’ shy about your degree.      I might’ve been lying shy, but I ain’t lying broken. Just not in a rush to be employed like a ‘duty of the working class.’ Is that a phrase now?      Probably. My mam says I’ve got three years, then it’s all backs to the grind whether I want to or not.

Rather annoying I had to cancel last Sunday’s gym buddy plan. Work had me tied down with that conference prep... What was I thinking signing up to coordinate events at 23?      Aw, it's all right. I understand the chaos of being a grown-up. Honestly, I’ve not een out the house properly this week. It’s like I’ve got this invisible thing callin’ me to stay in. Lazy, but blissful in a way, innit?      You should get out! Put on sommat decent and hit the park or somethin’. You won’t get fitter sittin’ on the Sofa Bullin’ Netflix at six in the mornin’.      You make it sound so left-right, like I’m gon nap-time for the D10 Qualifiers I’ll be training for. Truth be told, I’ve been working better on breakfasts—cereal bars and tea. Less effort for me. I’m not saying it’s fair, just that it’s possible to get back on. Ever thought of doing one of those online courses? Some basic project management or MS Office type certification? To be fair, I’ve done that ‘basic computing course’ lark a few years back to no great effect. Burgundy baked beans twice that week after passed out.      Ha, it's a start, innit? At least tried. I mean, I started out in the event world as a volunteer marshmallow of a co-ordinator with lunches delivered a couple of days late. Now I schedule 500-person conferences.      Maybe it is time go back to my pond life if you've had a real proper advancement.      I’m genuinely serious—apply for that course through the Job Centre. It could be something small, but it could begin a domino effect. And heck, maybe even we can find a gym buddy plan sometime that's over this.

Right then, lads, don't just sit there grinning. The dishes ain't going to clear up themselves, and I've had enough of this mess from the dinner! Chop, chop!      Yeah, come on lads, we’ve got a bit of a backlog here. Got a meeting tomorrow morning, and I’m not starting the day with dust bunnies in the kitchen.      Ugh, that sounds like a pain. Can’t we just get a robot or something? We’ve got all the tech for that now, surely.      Yeah, but they’re even more fiddly than me with my phone. One day they do a perfect job, the next they fall over and melon-burst themselves on the tiles!      Aye, and I’m not buying any of that fancy automated nonsense. My Maw used a breakfast plate and a duster to keep our house spotless in '73, and it worked! No fiddling, no nonsense—and no power sockets to unplug!      Speaking of nonsense, listen—did I tell you the story about that time I had to play tennis with my mate’s uncle in… what was it, Liverpool? Ten out of ten best burns. He showed up with a moustache, and I asked if it was new. He goes, “It’s been there seven years, mate. I’m just waiting for it to connect.”      Oh no, that’s grim. Why’d he have to keep it so long?      Don’t get started on beards and moustaches! Look at me—trying to grow about five days’ worth and it looks like the touchpaper of a mine. Not much cop.      Not like some people I could mention.      That’s for sure. If your girlfriend’s anything like mine, she’ll throw a shoe at the first sprout. ‘Bacteria farms,’ I tried to explain. She said I could stick the sprouts up somewhere that doesn’t get out in public!      You got a girlfriend? Since when? You never said anything!      Keep your voice down, or I’ll tell you about the time I tried to impress her at an Instagram café and ordered a ‘rainbow oats’—which turned out to be six different shades of beige!      Yeah, I’m onto your Instagram feed anyway. It’s just dad jokes and pictures of ‘dinner’ when it’s just a bag of noodles.      Speaking of, lads, I don’t want to hear about your Instagram followers or your girlfriend.

Rather annoying I had to take the back seats to the tip earlier. I was just trying to get rid of that old dining table, mind you. Looked more like a smugglers’ chest after twenty years! I remember sitting at  this  table and learning how to knit, only to rip it all out and re-do it four times because I couldn’t left-hand loop properly. Probably worth a fortune now, if it weren’t for the dent in the corner from your cousin Trevor, Maria.      Aye, that brat! Right, but moving on—Maria’s friend Jane and her partner are in quite a spot. That ghastly health something they’ve got. Dementia, is it goin’ on? Poor man looks like he’s walking through a dream half the time, but still insists on making the boxfile buns every morning.      Aye, and let’s not forget the beaver scouts’ Christmas party last December. True to life, we ended up with over thirty children’s food allergies and a missing marshmallow.

Rather annoying to be honest, Mump. I’ve been going mental trying to get my head around it. I got the email from work saying there’s going to be some redundancies, and I just don’t see it coming. Yep, I’ve got a shift at the gym on Saturday morning, then we were going to pop over to see Grandad at the care home in Norfolk. He misses you, you know. Any chance of a camping trip on the weekend after that, maybe with the boxset or something? Proper relaxation?      I can make it happen, if the weather is any kind to us.

I tried last year, but the bus broke down on the way and I ended up back in Bradford with an ice cream headache. Cats on the bus breakfast, no less. I hated it.      Blooming typical. I remember once, on a train near London, I thought I had my pyjamas in my bag, but no—it was a man’s knickers I packed by mistake. Left me with nothing but the clothes on my back in Brighton. Still—it wasn't  that  bad, was it?      Worse than that! Last summer, I tried to go camping in the Peaks. Now don’t laugh, but the phone app told me to turn left at the sheep. So I did. Next thing I know, my tent collapsed in a field of dandelions and I had a face full of something very green and very muddy. Not the holidays I wanted.      Haha, I about wet meself. That does sound baaaaad, though. I had a trip a few years back where I forgot my passport. I left everything behind—laptop, mobile, the lot—but I realized before I left the guesthouse. Still, it was quite the scramble.      Oh, I once left my sister at the hospital waiting room with a stick while I got a coffee. Took me 20 minutes trying to find her again. She was convinced the hospital took the stick back. Still don’t know where it went.      Mournin’ life if you ask me. Just give me a quiet weekend in the garden, a pot of tea, and the telly. No foreign airports, no lost sticks, no lost knickers—just a bit of BBC2 and peace.      Tell it like that and you might get the award for best holiday suggestion.

Rather annoying this, innit? That bloke at the back’s practically shouting in the telly. Mind you, the match’s not exactly gripping us today, eh? Not like we've seen over the years where it was all over the place. Look at that striker! C’mon, shoot!       laughs  Yeah, it’s   tosh  , basically. Proper turgid. I’ve only watched it because I fancied a bit of fish and chips after. Imagine me, pulling out the old tongs and the heatwave outside. Didn’t even want to walk past the chip shop earlier. It was like baked beans on the barbie, innit?      You like that Mytens, don’t you? Nah, I’m not surprised. I’m watching for the Dabba, and I’ll be honest, he’s barely in it. What’s he do for breakfast, eh? Wah? I mean, he’s playing in his basewi’ and looked like he hadn’t even brushed his teeth yet!      You mean Rashford? Hahah, I’ve seen better impacts in shortbread tins. But still, I tell ya, when the lads pull something out, it’s like rhythm and blues from the left. Though I can’t understand why Gary Neville doesn’t comment more these days. He used to give us somethin’ to listen to. Silly Stones is all we get now!      Aye, Spally’s alright. Just sounds like he wants to sell us a secondhand tennit court! Still, mind the marshmallows here—ain’t like watching  proper  football in the sixties, with the terraces roarin’ like the pubs lit up. Now it’s all burgers and sandwiches and not a bog standard pie to be seen.      That’s just it. Burgers and treacle scones passed out by stewards. I remember going as a nipper and being all fired up cos I got a decent custard cream. Now they’re handing out kale and lentils as though we’re in some health camp!      Not if the oysters at half-time are anything to go by. I swear, the away gooners get better food!      True innit? I’ll stick with the Maccy Ds or something when I can’t be arsed to cook. The chicken burger? Oh, it’s po’ cheap, but I’ll take it. Less like a waste of chips and more like a waste of time, if y’know what I mean.      Totally. I’ve started ordering in, to be fair. Thai or Chinese, somethin’ to keep the onions and fat from the slap-up Sunday roast at my mam’s.

Rather annoying the new films at the moment innit? Seems like everything wants to be a bit ‘glorified advert’ rather than proper storytelling. Remember when films actually told a story, like the ones we watched on the telly when we were younger, Gran?      Oh aye, they een’t the same, I’ll say that for 'em. Back in me day, we’d have a clean cloth on the TV screen and sit in this very spot, cup of tea and stew in front of us. Today’s lot, they blink too much an’ chase the camera about.      Right, I’ve even taken to skipping previews. Honestly, sometimes the ads are better than the film itself now. My son keeps saying I’ve lost me touch with youth culture, but I’d rather stick to what I know, like these sad but brilliant British dramas.      Yeah, but it’s a shame—there’s always something good if you dig for it. Me and the lads at work weeke to see those old stunt cyclist films once in a while, like Water Babies or something, get the kids in a tizzy about it.      Oh, I love those, love the bikes in them! You reckon you'd have time for that sort of film nowadays with all the meetings you have to do?      Hay, it’s the meetings somethin’ to write home about! You know what it’s like, every job we take’s a 'project' now. I swear, if I had my way, I'd run the whole thing on what you had to do at mum's tea factory back in ‘76 – crude but effective!      I daresay you wouldn't be standing the tea factory today, Charlie. Not with a clipboard an' a spreadsheet alike that.      Aye, well, if the bin lads could do it with colour-coded lorry routes, so can I. Just me way of it though – any bloody meeting I can have by phone, I’ll have by phone!      Right ho, as long as you don’t take lunches to a meeting again with your steak and kidney pie. That meeting room reeked for weeks!      That go bad or smog it up the whole place again – I ain't complainin‘, but that was a smell.      Anyway, all that aside. I was planning to make a nice Sunday roast one of these weeks. Properly feed the belly, not just a chip and a saucer over the telly like usual.

Rather skip the school assembly this year, love. Thought we do something different this Pancake Day. The kids have got to go to the Science Museum this week, and I fancy a day by the sea, ourselves. You two fancy that?      Can we go to Paris instead?      I like Paris!      We’ll think about it, Tom. But for now, let’s not argue. If you’re too fussy to finish your breakfast, you won’t be going to the museum at all. I’ve seen this before — when children don’t eat properly, they get fussy all day. Mary, do you like your pancakes today?      I like mine well done, like Grandpa’s! But I left the one you gave me, because I wanted to talk about the Green Knowe story. Did you know it's in the library?      Yes, I’ve read it a few times myself — in fact, it’s one of my favourites from my childhood in Dartford. There was a time I would read that by torchlight under the covers.      Can I read short stories too?      Of course, love. As long as you brush your teeth and wash your hands first. That way, no matter how exciting the book is, you’re still clean and ready for school. Also, I’ve been telling the class about children in other places who don’t get to read at all — so maybe this is a reminder not to waste your books or your meals.      I don’t understand what you mean.      Some children don’t even have enough food to eat, let alone books. So we should make the most of the privileges we have. Now, listen — this weekend, if youBehaviour well at school, we can see if the Festival Hall is doing any family events to do with science. And then, if the weather’s right, off to the beach.      Can Auntie Lila come?      Only if she promises not to crack my good dishes when I’m making crumpets. She nearly broke the set last time!      Was it when you said “Growing up is growing up!”, and she dropped the plate?      Precisely! But that was ages ago. Right, I need to get the box for the museum from the shed. Finish your toast — or I won’t help you pack your lunch for next week. And I don’t want to hear about Paris on an empty stomach.

Rather annoying that the sweet and sour chicken isn't as sweet as mine makes it. Should we order another round from the usual takeout or try something new?      I've been over this with you, Lucy. Not all Chinese restaurants have the same recipe! Besides, can't it be a good excuse to try that new place we passed on the way home? They had that banner up "Authentic Sichuan Cuisine." I'm game if you are.      Honestly, I'd dump the sweet and sour and just go for the Sichuan Mu Shu or the Mala spicy hotpot. It's been ages since I've had anything with a proper kick to it. Still, Alice, are you sure you're up for spicy? The last time you tried hot pot you cried on the bus.      I'll be fine! But if you lot all want the hot stuff, I can live with that. I just happened to miss a bit of variety at dinner, you know?      If I had a penny for every time someone said that—! Let’s just see what the new place has. Might be worth a punt. What did they say about grief support on the news today? That was something else. My neighbour lost his father, and the way it's all being handled—is it new rules or what?      Yeah, the headline was something like "Funeral customs evolving under new guidance." I glanced at it but zoned out—this is just someone else's problem for now. I’d read it tomorrow if I were you.      Also, have you seen the latest Bob the Builder? That show brings back so many memories! I still say about half the kids in the playgroup can quote the whole "Can we fix it?" line by heart. My sister is obsessed.      Honestly, we should all go. My housemate Angela is desperate to go out. All she does is scroll on her phone and clean the bathroom religiously. She's practically a nun.      Angela, the one who screams at dust bunnies as though they’re personal insults? Please, keep her indoors with bleach and a mop. Not all of us remember a time before sanitiser.      Let's not get snarky. How about a film night after Chinese? I’ve just got that new release with the boxset vibe films.      So long as it’s not another murder mystery with someone in every episode pretending to fall off a cliff, I’m in.

Rather do I! The other day, I swiped a banana glue sticks and her recipe cards scattered everywhere. It got to the point she insisted on dining at the kitchen table, saying it was the only place where she thought the sun “possibly wouldn’t find the mess.”        coordinates again and beginning to plan a weekend bicycle ride with the dog. I reckon his wife's all for that, but you’ve only got to ask her once and she’s got a whole list of “preparations” she’s got to do before the bike comes out. Didn’t even want to know what he thought of my frozen peas jokes. Still, it made me smile, as he said, “Well, at least the dog eats what’s on his plate.”      Ah, I well know the sentiment, jeune Darcy, I used to make the world’s best rice krispy cakes when Mabel was small. She’d sit at the kitchen table, with a little apron on and furiously stirring as if she were some great confectioner of the 18th century. I still chuckle when I remember the time I forgot to take the rusk out of the oven to let it cool. Mabel tried to open the oven and—well, it wasn’t a little explosion, but it most certainly shook the kitchen chair she was sitting in!      Honestly, the memories you two make me laugh out loud. Earlier this week, I went into the grocery store for a packet of coffee and someone bumped into me. Big mistake! All my coffee spilled everywhere, and I had a hapless gentleman from the isle behind me trying to give me money as if I’d  actually  spent it! He nearly about fainted when I pulled the coffee out from my bag and said “No, I just wanted to see if you were that good at paying for things while absent-minded.”      That reminds me of the new “scan as you go” thing. The other day, I finished my shopping and was holding my phone trying to find the QR code for the till station. We had to wait as some poor soul in front of us was trying to find his phone and ended up balancing the groceries he’d scanned in his hands  and  a Smart Cart like it was a bowling set go-kart on wheels.      You young ones and your modern marvels.

Rather annoying the wet weather, eh? You’d think in Rome we’d have a bit more  character  than nonstop rain. I mean, I’m more than happy to take a cappuccino and a view of the Colosseum, not a puddle and a sneeze.      Yeah, I understand the hype, but I haven’t seen the sun all week. Though I’ve been working from my flat—much more comfortable than a damp B&B. The AirBnB place is great, though. Super central. You lot should come check it out.      Oh, I’ve seen it! Massive compared to some of the ones I’ve stayed in. I managed to get one of those typical old Roman apartments—you know the ones, stone floors, creaky stairs, but with a killer view of the Aventine Hill. It’s far enough out that you’re not breakfasting to the sound of horns and scooters.      I hear you, love that vibe, even if it's a bit tough to find. I’ve been working over at this place near the Spanish Steps. Mate takes care of two baristas a week to keep things human. Kinda like a rotating cast of… well, barista extraordinaire, from what I hear. Ha – Mate’s been at it for, like, six weeks now.      Now don’t go making him sound indispensable. If I book a table at Trattoria Roma tonight, you all must come. It’s a bit of a trek, a bit of a trek, but the lamb shank—absolute game-changer.      Can’t promise I won’t end up in a food coma. I’m baking a new sourdough recipe for my cafe this week. It’s wild, this city—you know that Bread & Wine spot near the Pantheon? They’re charging €10 for a toastie. Madness!      Well, I’m open to a bit of extravagance every now and again. I’ve been helping my little sister sort out her dorm room back in Birmingham. You’d think a young woman her age’d figure a little decor out by now, but the concept of  continuity  eludes her.      That’s the best I ever heard about your family, love. Anyone else made plans beyond this? I’m figuring out if I’ve got enough holiday left to zip to Hobart for New Year’s. Smells of kelp and kangaroos, eh?      Oh right on! I’ve got a mate down there—Meg—who runs a little eco lodge.

So, I just wanted to bring up the whole hen do thing. I know it's still a bit early, but I've been thinking about it a lot more lately. I mean, Ali is getting married next year, and we need to do something  amazing ! I wouldn't say it was my idea, but I sort of brought it up with the group chat the other day.      Oh yes! A big one. I think doing a weekend away might be easier since Ali works quite a bit and it’s always hard to get her full attention. Didn’t you want to do something with crafts too?      Yeah! I’ve been into baking lately and thought maybe we could do some kind of weekend where we mix crafts and cooking with some girly bonding. I’ve been following some DIY influencer pages on Instagram, and I think there are some local workshops that do both baking and macramé. I could probably even teach them to make some mini cupcakes for the morning!      Wait, I’m ordering the cakes and the coffee. That’s my role, right? I do like the idea of something cozy rather than the typical bar crawl. Like a “recharging the human soul” kind of vibe.      GIRL YES! I was just thinking about that. We can’t do a hen do without some personal stuff because Ali’s not huge on the typical partying. But if we do something at home or a rented farmhouse, maybe with brunch-type stuff and some coffee bar someone sets up in the living room?      That sounds oddly feasible. I was thinking about the Rosie and Ali Bonds venue as a central point. Not the big house, maybe a studio nearby? I did some research last week and found a few places that offer all-inclusive “girly weekend packages.” They include coffee setups, baking classes, and even a bit of yoga in the mornings.      Oh, that’s high-end! But Ali would love it. I know it’s a bit out of our regular budget, but if we split the cost with the group, maybe we could do something over the autumn. Her anniversary comes with lunches and a little “hype up wedding” schedule, but October sounds doable.      I could even set up the room on my own if we don’t get a venue. I’ve been doing digital mockups for events lately—maybe I can create a layout and some virtual invites.

Rather annoying I caught flu just as I was meant to go on that trip to Malaga, innit? I got the email from the hotel saying I’m sorted for a room with a view      Aww, honestly that seems like a dodgy move on their part. Ain’t you always een? I thought you wanted to take some loose time and enjoy the Med      I did yeah, but I think I’m more grateful I got to avoid the chaos of checking in while pulling through a fever and cough. My brother’s here at the oven when he isn’t bloinkin’ off on his Xbox      Well, as long as you’re still likin’ the company and the turkey curry. You’ve already enough to deal with without this backrache-chips-and-blob-on-the-surface business      It is alright, the kitchen is better than breakfast, no doubt. I just happened to volunteer after I saw his cooking routine, you ever looked at that? He pushes puff pastry into the microwave and talks to it      Ha, maybe it is better than nothing. I mean if you land a edible meal and don’t get sent to hospital, then bravo on both accounts      Speak for yourself. I remember the last time you got the hiccups, you tried to confirm it was the gas and nearly blew up the whole place with the induction hob      That was a one-off, was someone not in the mood? Let me not read too much into it. I mean I can give you a rundown on some hotel in Florence I want to review next month if you fancy      I about blocked out Florence after eating the same bolognese five nights in a row. Honestly what is this cuisine? They take the same sauce and serve it with lasagne, ravioli, spaghetti, for tres fois      I know, that’s why I reckoned it’d be something fresh, I mean with a farm to table idea or something. My brother-in-law is looking to stay over as well, but space is limited. Would you allow it?      My knees are sore, I can’t travel or host the dinner, but go ahead. I’ll see if I can procure some real ramen or bratwurst for recovery between these soddin’ infusions      Cool, just take flu seriously, innit? I’ve seen colleagues down with it for weeks because they wouldn’t rest.

Rather annoying when the birthday cards get my age wrong, isn't it? I'm fifty-two, not fifty-three or fifty-four! And no, I’m not letting my age stop me from having a proper day out, thank you very much.      It's the same with me — my card last time said sixty  three , even though I'm   just   sixty-one! It's like these shops just throw numbers in at random. I've started writing my details inside the cards now, just in case someone buys it and can't be bothered to check. Didn’t your card come with a lovely purple calendar fob, by the way?      Yes, the purple one was rather fetching — and very well-padded, too. I’m still thinking of putting one of the calendars I get from the charity shop on it, and I’ll be sure to label it with both names and dates. Speaking of shopping, I made a list earlier this week. Eggs, bread, cheese — the usual. But I also thought, you know, I should get a new pair of gardening gloves. Mine are falling apart.      Oh, I might put that on your list as well. Did I tell you, by the way, that I’ve been volunteering at the computing museum in Leeds lately? It's lovely – such fascinating old machines. I helped a young chap set up an exhibition on the early history of home computers.      Oh, that's lovely! I might pop along and have a look. I remember doing art and craft at school — knitting, painting, building oddly-shaped birds out of pipe cleaners! Still have a shoebox full of it somewhere. Margate Primary had such a good crafts room. I did make a rather nice birdcage out of broken matchsticks, though I’m ashamed to say the bird escaped.      I remember it more as a place to dodge the bin, personally! But I treasured my teacher — passed away a few years ago, poor soul. I used to pass on all my old computer bits to the museum, little Arduinos and the like. Those were fun to mess around with before they became the 'thing'. I wonder what my students would say if they knew I set up a Raspberry Pi.      Oh, go on then — tell them about your antiques. Just don’t expect me to follow, I’m afraid. I tried a recording course at the uni once, but you could sum it all up as “press this button, then that button”.

Rather annoying the new neighbours, eh, love? That lot opposite—never know if it’s ‘normal’ when they’re out with binoculars every Sunday, observing birds! Mind, I think the chap's a twitcher. Not quite my idea of a quiet afternoon!      But it’s all right, really. Gives the place some colour. Still, better than the noisy couples that were there before. A lot less shouting now, that's for sure.      Honestly, you should be grateful we’ve got decent neighbours for once! The Wilsons don’t seem at all bad. I’ve chatted with Mary a few times. She’s lovely and offered to show me how to grow marjoram since I keep struggling with my herb garden.      Yes, I do love a bit of gardening. The sunlight this morning made my jasmine in the conservatory smell amazing! And I see you've started painting the spare room, H drive in there yet? I lent you that brush rack, didn’t I?      Aye, I’ve got it here, yes. Rather sturdy, that one I borrowed off you. Got as far as the walls last week, but still need to tackle the ceiling. Doesn’t seem quite right when it’s left undone.      I’ve got a bit of time this weekend, if you want help. It might go quicker than you trying to do the ceilings and walls in one go. Saves those ceiling drops going all soggy and dripping on the carpet. Trust me, I’ve done it!      Fair enough. I’d be grateful. Still, this new place has its perks, eh? Not nearly as far from the mainline as I thought. Got the 7:22 from Exeter now and not that bad of a journey.      That's true. My sister’s planning to visit from London soon. She passed through here once on the trains and said the views between Exeter and Plymouth are worth it. Guess it’s a little slower than the previous regional services we had.      He knows the train journey a little better than I do, but the recent work delays irk me something rotten. Picked up the local paper last night—some line cleaning up improvements near Exeter St David’s station. I do hope it means fewer delays.      Aye, well, you two could have a little trip to Exeter and leave me to my ceiling! I’ll just belly up to the pub on Saturday night, get over this painting malaise and see if the new barman has my usual pint ready.

Rather annoying this, innit? I tried to order me some glue sticks online for the ‘obby mends... got the email saying they’re shipping now, yet it’s still not arrived.      Aye, them delivery times are a nightmare sometimes! I wouldn’t rely on it turnin’ up before Saturday, I reckon.      Naw, I wanted them for next week. I ‘ave a flat tyre t’fix and I need sumfink t’secure it properly. This doin’ nothin’ but sittin’ ‘round messin’ wi’ me... like, I’ve even tried fixin’ jobs wi’ no tools, but still somethin’s fallin’ apart.      Yeah, I feel that. I’m constantly fixin’ them holes in me tent in the garden now. Living with uni rent’s a laugh sometimes!      I’d kill for a decent kitchen in me place. I’ve got sumfink muck-in’ up the sink again. One time, I thought I’d bin the plug, but it turns out it was still powered up and the whole room flooded.      Oh, sounds like me when I tried messin’ wi’ the washing machine. I turned it off but it still got misted up and I had to call a bloke. Cost me nearly £100!      ‘Ow d’you pay for all that? ‘ave you still got spare cash after uni stuff?      I manage with part-time shifts at the café in Egremont and ‘course, I’ve had to cut back on stuff. I do miss ‘avin’ a proper date night though.      I wish I ‘ad some part-time work to plug me up wi’ anyway. ‘Ere I am binning ‘ousehold jobs like no tomorrow, but I can’t even get a Signals duster job.      That’s a real shame. I spoke to me mum t’other day and she said they’ve ‘ad loads of people quitting recently, so maybe it’s ‘opeful?      I’m runnin’ out o’ hope by the go. I get offered work if I’m not even applying. Genuinely sick of the whole loop between applyin’, rejection, then waitin’ ‘fore tryin’ sumfink else.      I know what you mean. I’m sick of workin’ for minimum wage ‘cause I’m not skilled enough. But I’m tellin’ mysel’ to stick t’uni. Gotta plan for the future, innit?      ‘Ere, want somethin’ from Amazon before it goes mad again? I can do a bit of a browse on me phone for ideas while me kettle boils.      Aye, I do need nexmonth’s phone billin’ payed.

Rather annoying this new house isn't it? That contractor gave us everything we wanted, but it's not like it's turned out exactly how we dreamt it would. I can't say I'm over the moon about the floorboards, honestly.      It's a great base, though. We just need to sort out the flooring and paint the walls. I reckon it's going to be absolutely adorable once we’ve got all the furniture in and everything's settled in.      I agree, it's a nice enough place. I did wonder what you're thinking about the heating system. You don’t like to fiddle much, so maybe we should get a smart thermostat? I read that they can make a bit of a difference in the long run.      Smart thermostats – I've heard them mentioned, and I think they look like a fad if you ask me. All the buttons and apps—good heavens, I just want to turn the thing up and stay warm. But if you lot fawn over them so much, I suppose I could give it a go.      We can install one together if you want! It’s not as complicated as you might think.      Well… I reckon I'd rather take a walk along the coast than fiddle with gadgets. Speaking of which, I read that there's a long stretch of the coast path not too far from here. Seems like a perfect way to get some fresh air and maybe spot a few dolphins out on the water.      That does sound lovely, Alan. I do love a good walk—especially with a decent stretch of sea and hill in between. I might bring my camera along, it could be a nice place to take a few pictures.      Alright then. Let’s plan for Saturday morning. I’m thinking we take the trail near the headland first—should be a fairly manageable route for you both. And if we’re lucky, maybe we can grab a bite at that cafe mentioned on the map.      Perfect. After that, we could come back and start shopping for the furniture. I've been looking at a couple of spots online—there’s a fairly good place in Exeter, I think.      Oh, goody! I could do with getting some new shelves for my books.      I suppose we could go with a modest budget, what with all of us contributing.

Rather skip the dishes and just go through to the sofa, do you?      Oh, come on, love, you're one to talk after  that  mess you made in the kitchen this morning with the ingredients for your smoothie. You nearly frightened the cat.      Right, okay, I’ll admit it was a bit of a farce involving a blender that clearly has a vendetta against me. But I managed! I got it right in the end. It had banana, spinach, and pistachio protein powder for a change. Apparently, that’s what you need to get through three more months of mostly sitting in a lab and talking about the stresses of elderly patients.      Just don’t expect melon and lime next week. Ten to one you’ll accidentally toss in some peppermint and I’ll be the one explaining to the in-laws why Mummy won’t breakfast with us for a week this time.      Blooming hell, not again. I swear to God I told the in-laws I would  calm down , and here you are encouraging me to listen to their criticisms again like some broken record. They still don’t get why I’ve still not moved on from my PhD, do they?      No, and Mate, you don’t have to prove yourself to them. You’ve got the paper published in  Health Psychology Quarterly , and you're doing work that could genuinely help people. Rather annoying this new eligibility criteria for universal credit, isn't it? But I remember when I was younger, they were always promising to support older people, and now it’s like it’s just another cut here and a tax there.      Honestly, I don’t like to complain, but these changes—especially with housing benefit—are making people desperate. I’ve had tenants like that at the childminder home I used to run. Families qualified just by the skin of their teeth, and suddenly, one extra person or a little rise in housing costs, and the whole balance shifts. It’s no way to run a country, asking people for money while at the same time pulling the rug from under them.      That’s exactly it. It’s contradictory and it doesn’t make sense. I listen to the occasional news on the telly, and you’d think the economy was roaring, but from where I’m sitting, it feels like it’s all just window dressing. It’s all politicians wanting to look like they’re doing something, but when it really matters, they save the rich and gold-plate the middle classes while the poor get squeezed.      Oh, I know! I mean, it’s not like we’re the first generation to say this. But it feels like things have only gotten worse. And now with all the TV shows pushing this ‘get back to work’ mantra, you’d think anyone on benefits is just shirking and lazy. Nonsense. People want dignity, but what I see are systems designed to break their spirits, not build them up.      I agree with you there. Look at my son-in-law—hard worker, but one injury and he was out of work, had to rely on support while he recovered.

Rather annoying this wet weather, eh? You know, in Cambridge we’d have just wrapped up with a nice cup of tea and some quiet reading. Ten days in bed watching reruns of  Doctor Who  and eating lukewarm soup—hardly glamorous, but hey, better than breakfast with my old uncle at this time. Maybe we should’ve just ordered pesto pasta and a couple of gins from some high-street chain. Just like, life’s too short for establishment poetry and overpriced bread rolls, innit?
